title: A FLOOR IS A BOUND, AND A BOUND MAY ONLY TIGHTEN
frozen_text: Where a threshold is derived from repeated measurement, its declaration must state its kind. A quantity declared BOUND is combined across ensembles by taking the worst observed excursion, and may move only in the conservative direction as ensembles accumulate. A quantity declared ESTIMATE is combined by a rule declared before the second ensemble is run, and may move in either direction. A quantity with no declared kind may not be used in a gate. A combining rule chosen after the measurements it combines is admissible only where every candidate rule LEGALLY AVAILABLE UNDER THE LAW IN FORCE AT THE MOMENT OF CHOICE yields the same disposition. Availability is a property of the law, not of the executor's enumeration: a candidate the law already forbade is not made available by being named, and a candidate the law permitted is not made unavailable by a refusal issued afterwards. The record must name each candidate, state for each whether it was available and under which prior ruling, and record the agreement across the available set as the reason for admissibility.
what_changed: the admissibility clause is REPLACED. The prior draft read 'every candidate rule available at the moment of choice', which left availability to be read off the executor's enumeration; the replacement makes availability a property of the law and states both directions — naming does not confer it, and a later refusal does not remove it
